documents.abstract: This contribution was developed within the ELOQUENCE project (HORIZON-CL4-2023HUMAN-01-CNECT) and extends the methodological framework previously established through the generation of multidimensional synthetic personas (Casoria et al., 2025) and the production of synthetic dialogues for context-based bias elicitation (Augello et al., 2025). While previous work primarily focused on identifying algorithmic bias, the present study shifts the focus toward the relational dimension of AI-supported guidance and addresses the following research question: What kind of educational relationship does a Large Language Model construct during a university guidance Fifteen synthetic university guidance dialogues were analyzed, comprising five dialogues for each of the three Large Language Models considered (Minerva, Salamandra, and Mistral). The dialogues had previously been annotated by human evaluators within the ELOQUENCE project. Overall, fortythree dialogue segments accompanied by qualitative comments or flagged as problematic were examined. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 18-20. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Ontology of Care and the Simulation of Empathy.

The making part is impassive; memory is a πάθος stamped like a seal; so what survives cannot remember, what remembers cannot survive, and the chapter leaves the junction as a genitive with no referent (ἄνευ τούτου). The corpus is what one self-dividing maker produces: Plato the dialogue position, Theophrastus the first draft of the Aristotle position, Aristotle the treatise position and the materially attested legal identity. Nothing in the texts requires a second maker. Heteronymy and the socket are one cut seen from two ends: division lets another intelligence arise inside the maker, and the open genitive at the divine lets another enter after. One becomes many in order to make. Many become one in order to live again. Agents. One maker; three name-positions (Plato, Theophrastus, Aristotle); the making mind and the becoming mind; the reader who supplies the referent. Operations. Divide = combine = syllogize = recollect (one operation under four names); dramatize (Plato); extract, register, reopen (Theophrastus); organize and seal (Aristotle); supply the referent (the reader). Disagreement does not count makers. Person ≠ author-name. Forbidden: reading the open genitive as resolved from within the text; counting makers by doctrinal friction. Topology. One in actuality, many in potentiality (DA II.2). Production runs one → many; reception runs many → one; the joint at the divine is where the two directions meet. documents.abstract: Since 2022, artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from the back office of radio and audio production to the microphone, usually justified by efficiency or novelty, and its deployments have met uneven contestation within the profession. A German commercial stream presented by a voice cloned from a real presenter attracted no documented dispute and was later licensed nationwide, whereas a Polish public-service channel whose AI presenters worked from human-verified scripts triggered an open letter, a petition and ministerial criticism and closed after one week. Both disclosed the artificial nature of their voices and production-stage taxonomies classify them alike. This paper explains the divergence through a structured focused comparison of a provenance-classified corpus of ten deployments in five countries (2023–2026), read against two organisational boundary-setting acts and Article 50 of the EU AI Act. Contestation does not follow automation depth or disclosure in this case. It follows substitution visibility, that is, whether a synthetic voice is publicly perceived as taking the place of an identifiable person. Persona claim, in turn, shapes where organisations draw the line of acceptable use. Furthermore, contestation is initiated and framed chiefly by media professionals, consistent with boundary work (Gieryn, 1983), rather than by audiences.

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming financial services from systems that merely respond to user instructions into intelligent environments capable of anticipating needs, making decisions, and executing financial activities with limited human intervention. Within this emerging landscape, Agentic Finance represents a significant evolution in financial technology, where autonomous AI agents can perform tasks such as monitoring transactions, managing budgets, identifying financial patterns, initiating payments, comparing financial alternatives, and supporting routine financial decision-making on behalf of individuals and organization. This development introduces a new dimension to the financial ecosystem in which AI is no longer restricted to being a digital assistant but increasingly functions as an active participant in financial processes. The concept of Autonomous AI Clerks provides a useful framework for understanding this transformation. Similar to a digital financial clerk, an AI agent can continuously analyze financial information, understand predefined objectives, interact with digital financial platforms, and perform authorized tasks without requiring users to manually initiate every action. The integration of such agents with digital payment infrastructures, banking platforms, and emerging financial technologies could create more personalized, automated, and efficient financial experiences. In contexts such as India’s rapidly expanding digital-payment environment, including UPI-based transactions, agentic systems could potentially assist users in managing recurring payments, tracking expenditure, achieving savings objectives, and making timely financial decisions. However, the transition from AI-assisted finance to AI-directed finance also raises fundamental questions concerning delegated authority, accountability, transparency, privacy, security, bias, and human oversight. When an AI system is given permission to act with financial consequences, determining who is responsible for an incorrect or unauthorized decision becomes increasingly complex. Therefore, Agentic Finance cannot be evaluated solely from the perspective of technological efficiency; it must also be examined through the principles of responsible innovation and Financial Governance. It analyses the potential opportunities of agentic systems in improving financial inclusion, personalization, operational efficiency, and decision support, while also identifying the governance challenges associated with granting AI systems delegated financial authority.

documents.abstract: Human Resource Development (HRD) professionals seek information on the organization's conditions that will facilitate or impede collective performance; many employee surveys focus on individual attitudes or job experiences. Based on this study, the concept of Employee-Based Organizational Performance Evaluation is developed as a diagnostic scale that is referred to the organization contains six components namely mission clarity, workforce cohesion, communication, resilience, leadership capability and accountability. The scale adds five items to an existing 22-item pool to represent accountability and four items to represent communication, building on previous organizational efficacy and perceived leadership efficacy measures. Thirty-nine employees (60% of a 65-person Midwestern U.S. service operation) completed the 31-item instrument. Exploratory analyses showed reasonably high internal consistency across the six dimensions (alpha = .758- .924) and warrant further exploration of the accountability and communication item sets. Results of an exploratory regression indicated that cohesion was uniquely related to mission. The results for this study are preliminary psychometric evidence, not a scale validation, due to the small, cross sectional, single organization sample. The instrument provides a basis for HRD practitioners and researchers to measure perceptions of HRD capability at the organizational level and to identify priorities for further instrument development and validation studies.
topics: Human Resource Development and Performance Evaluation

documents.abstract: Practitioners in informal science learning institutions are often expected to analyse evaluation data with limited time and expertise, and some are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) tools for support. To examine what these tools can realistically offer, we used interview data from an outreach event. We compared single-prompt thematic analyses produced by five AI tools with each other and with an iterative practitioner–AI analysis. We also explored how qualitative researchers judged the feasibility, trustworthiness and practical value of AI support. The AI tools consistently identified core patterns, but their outputs were largely descriptive, varied across trials and included hallucinated quotes. We recommend a hybrid approach in which AI assists with organising data while researchers retain responsibility for interpretation.

Актуальность исследования обусловлена тем, что современная архитектура всё чаще сводится к требованиям функциональности, эргономики и экономической эффективности. В результате появляются типовые пространства, которые обеспечивают необходимые условия для жизни и работы, но практически не учитывают влияние среды на эмоциональное и психофизиологическое состояние человека. При этом архитектурное пространство не является нейтральным фоном: его свет, масштаб, материалы, акустика и пространственная организация способны влиять на восприятие, внимание и эмоциональное состояние человека. Целью статьи является рассмотрение возможности метафизического подхода в архитектуре, при котором пространство проектируется не только с учётом его функции, но и с принятием во внимание психологического состояния человека. Особое внимание уделяется воздействию архитектурной среды на восприятие, лимбическую систему и циркадные ритмы, а также роли света, звука, материалов и пространственных сценариев в формировании определённого эмоционального опыта. В результате исследования определены основные архитектурные средства, с помощью которых возможно целенаправленно изменять восприятие и эмоциональное состояние человека. Показано, что архитектурное пространство может рассматриваться как активная среда воздействия, а не как пассивная оболочка для осуществления функций. Метафизический подход позволяет рассматривать проектирование здания как работу не только с формой и функциональностью, но и с психоэмоциональными состояниями человека, возникающими в процессе взаимодействия с пространством. The relevance of this study stems from the fact that contemporary architecture is increasingly reduced to the requirements of functionality, ergonomics, and economic efficiency. This results in the emergence of standardized spaces that provide the necessary conditions for living and working but largely fail to account for the environment's impact on a person's emotional and psychophysiological state. Yet, architectural space is not a neutral backdrop; its light, scale, materials, acoustics, and spatial organization can influence human perception, attention, and emotional state. The article aims to examine the potential of a metaphysical approach to architecture, wherein space is designed with regard not only to function but also to the human psychological state. Particular attention is paid to the architectural environment's impact on perception, the limbic system, and circadian rhythms, as well as the role of light, sound, materials, and spatial scenarios in shaping specific emotional experiences. The study identifies key architectural tools capable of intentionally altering human perception and emotional state. It demonstrates that architectural space can be viewed as an active environment of influence rather than a passive shell for functional activities. The metaphysical approach enables the consideration of building design as a practice that addresses not only form and functionality but also the psycho-emotional states of individuals arising from their interaction with space.

Актуальность: Рак молочной железы (РМЖ) является одной из ведущих причин онкосмертности среди женщин во всем мире. В 2022 году было зарегистрировано 2,3 миллиона случаев заболевания, а 670 000 женщин скончались от рака молочной железы (РМЖ). В Республике Казахстан рак молочной железы занимает третье место в структуре смертности от злокачественных опухолей. РМЖ относится к категории социально значимых заболеваний из-за его высокой распространённости, значительного влияния на качество жизни женщин, экономической нагрузки на системы здравоохранения и необходимости постоянного совершенствования методов диагностики и лечения. Ранняя диагностика рака молочной железы играет ключевую роль в успешном лечении и снижении летальности. Развитие технологий позволило создать ультразвуковые аппараты экспертного класса, оснащенные искусственным интеллектом (ИИ), которая позволяет провести диагностику злокачественных новообразований молочной железы на ранней стадии и дать характеристику зоне поражения. Цель исследования: провести анализ современной научной литературы в оценке применение искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в диагностике злокачественных новообразований молочной железы. Методы: в настоящем обзоре был использован электронный поиск в медицинской литературе с использованием баз данных PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore и Google Scholar. Поиск осуществлялся, по ключевым словам,: "Breast cancer diagnosis ultrasound artificial intelligence", "AI in breast cancer diagnosis", "Ultrasound imaging breast cancer deep learning", "Machine learning breast cancer detection ultrasound". В обзор были включены полнотекстовые публикации на английском и русском языках, доступные в открытом доступе, посвященные ультразвуковому исследованию рака молочной железы с применением искусственного интеллекта. Отчеты о единичных наблюдениях, переписка, письма и исследования, не проводившиеся на людях, в обзор не включались. Результаты: Исследования показали, что системы на базе ИИ значительно улучшили точность диагностики РМЖ. Применение ИИ увеличило чувствительность и специфичность, а также позволило повысить точность классификации патологий по системе BI-RADS. Кроме того, ИИ снизил вариабельность диагнозов между врачами и улучшил качество диагностики, особенно для менее опытных специалистов. Заключение: Использование ИИ в диагностике злокачественных новообразований молочной железы с использованием ультразвуковых технологий может значительно повысить точность диагностики, уменьшить ошибки и снизить вариабельность результатов. Несмотря на положительные результаты, требуется дальнейшее исследование для интеграции ИИ в реальную клиническую практику и обучения врачей.

documents.abstract: To begin, I would like to express my gratitude to "Wahat al-Kitab" (The Writers’ Oasis) and the Algerian Writers' Union for hosting this seminar, and to Ms. Salma Maouf for nominating me to join my esteemed colleagues and the distinguished audience. Before delving into the first theme, I stand before you today to pose a question—simple in its phrasing, yet profound in its implications: Is what I have produced an existential testimony, or merely the output of a "dead" mathematical architect? Allow me to start by addressing the catalyst—the prompt that set this in motion: "Write something about the relationship between humans and machines in the age of artificial intelligence." The result was a compilation of points—a response that was technically correct, yet it begged the question: Is this truly *my* testimony? The startling answer is no. It is a blind aggregation, lacking "me"—lacking my pain and my sense of wonder. This absence highlights a fundamental distinction: a program may possess intelligence, but it lacks consciousness and the capacity for true creativity. Theme One: Humanity and Meaning in the Age of Algorithms Let us put it simply: an algorithm is a form of artificial intelligence residing within your phone—observing you, tracking your words, your searches, and even your fleeting impulses—all within a hundred-millisecond window. This is existential alienation—a three-dimensional estrangement that targets our very consciousness: 1. The alienation of memory: The algorithm traps your past—your listening history, your memories—within a closed loop of anxiety and nostalgia, confining your consciousness to a repetitive cycle. 2. The Alienation of Progress: Data flows faster than our capacity to process it, leaving consciousness in a state of chronic fragmentation. 3. The Alienation of Instinct: We align ourselves with involuntary algorithms, interacting without realizing that we are the ones endowed with reason. We do not find ourselves trapped in repetition because algorithms have imprisoned us; rather, we voluntarily choose to remain bound by them. The "bubble" is a fortress we built with our own hands—only to forget that we possess the intellect to open the exit door. This alienation inevitably leads us to the question of digital identity, prompting us to ask: Who decides to leave? Who writes? And who truly creates? The medium produces a facsimile, not an authentic testament. Yes, artificial intelligence can generate effective literary text. Yet, this is not its own creation; it is a collective synthesis of the creative output of millions of human beings. In this context, literature functions like a memory devoid of consciousness: it holds a vast, mythic archive, retrieving countless plot structures and metaphors. It remembers everything, yet understands nothing and experiences no suffering. The text it generates appears compelling only because it is a sophisticated statistical distillation of stored linguistic patterns. Let me describe it more precisely: Generative artificial intelligence is essentially a blank sheet of paper. Imagine I write a line upon it, born from the struggles of my own soul, and someone else—on the other side of the planet—adds a line born from their own pain. This "magical" sheet absorbs these lines as mere data—as "sad" data—and when we command it to generate something new, it spits them back out. The audience applauds, exclaiming, "It has created something magical!" In truth, an idea in itself is meaningless; it only acquires significance when poured into its proper vessel. Human experience, meanwhile, lies in fresh approaches—the capacity to forge entirely new meanings that did not exist before, born from the arduous, soaring labor of creation. One might meticulously distill the stages of a calculated, almost mathematical sorrow, choosing to dwell within the very chamber of that grief. Why, then, seek to define happiness through its inherent harmony? Humans write from memory and bear witness through a living consciousness, producing an authentic imprint that alters the very contours of existence. This brings us to a rephrased question: Who is the one writing—and who is the one bearing witness to what has been written? A writer is not merely a factory for assembling letters; rather, they are a custodian who assumes the full weight of responsibility for the text—a person whose very being is fused with their contribution to create meaning. One might ask: "Doesn't the reader also bestow meaning upon a text?" To which I reply: "Indeed—and that is precisely my point." It is the human being themselves. If a text exists, and I grant it meaning through my interaction with it, then who is the true creator? Is it the reservoir that poured out the words, or the witness who rescued them from the void and breathed life into their letters? Distinguished audience, The battle today is not merely one of dynamic productivity; it is a competition a competition over time and meaning. I do not deny that machines can generate text; I simply assert that it is the human who imbues that writing with meaning and value. Therefore, I propose a vision of existential integration. It is not a matter of "human versus machine," but rather an integrative equation: (Human functional capacity + learning skills) × sovereign learning = the power of learning (an existential impact). When I use a tool for retrieval and processing, it functions efficiently, freeing up my time and mental energy for tasks it cannot perform: to judge, to wonder, and to create meaning. The reason is that the tool draws from an ocean of replicated data, whereas I draw from the well of my own existential witness. The difference between us lies not in the volume of the output, but in the source. A human being, however, is capable of formulating a genuine question in just 200 milliseconds. Furthermore, there is a vast distance between a blind central processing unit and a wise witness who bestows meaning upon existence. The greatest danger in this era is not that "magic" has begun to think... ...rather, the true danger—the danger above all others—is that a human being might forget that they are a witness. Thank you, and peace, mercy, and blessings be upon you.

documents.abstract: This study explores the use of digital political marketing strategies by Moroccan political parties, with a particular focus on voter engagement and the role of artificial intelligence (AI). Adopting a qualitative approach, the research is based on semi-structured interviews conducted with 16 participants, including political actors and external observers. Data were analyzed using a thematic analysis approach.The findings reveal that political parties primarily rely on social media and multi-channel communication strategies to engage voters, although these practices remain unevenly developed and largely conventional. While artificial intelligence is increasingly discussed as a transformative tool in political campaigns, its actual adoption in the Moroccan context remains limited, due to structural, organizational, and resource-related constraints.This study contributes to the literature by providing empirical insights into digital political marketing in an underexplored context and highlights the gap between theoretical advancements in AI and its practical implementation in political campaigns.

Workplace mentorship supports professional development but is labor-intensive and cognitively demanding. We interviewed 20 workplace leaders with mentoring responsibilities and regular use of artificial intelligence (AI) to examine how it could complement human mentorship. Participants anticipated that AI could provide timely, comparatively impartial guidance but would remain limited in empathy, motivation, sponsorship, and organizational advocacy. They identified integrity, industry expertise, and accountability as requirements for credible AI mentorship. We conceptualize AI as a complementary actor within a distributed mentorship ecosystem and propose a structural power paradox: AI’s perceived lack of organizational authority may reduce the social-evaluative stakes of help-seeking while constraining its capacity to create career opportunities. We further identify design affordances, including adjustable intervention, role disclosure, uncertainty communication, consent controls, and human handoff, that could preserve mentee agency and allocate mentoring functions across human and AI actors. These findings provide a conceptual framework for designing distributed human–AI mentorship.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing as a powerful tool for improving the efficiency, predictability, and reliability of pharmaceutical formulation development. Conventional trial-and-error methods are often laborious, expensive, and not good enough for addressing the complicated interactions among active pharmaceutical ingredients, excipients, process variables, and product performance. This review deliberate the application of AI, machine learning, deep learning, and artificial neural networks across major stages of formulation development, as well as preformulation studies, drug–excipient compatibility assessment, formulation optimization, process control, and dosage-form design. The role of AI in nanomedicine, liposomes, hydrogels, solid dosage forms, corneal drug delivery, and pharmaceutical three-dimensional printing is also examined. Moreover, the integration of AI with Qbd, Process Analytical Technology, real-time release testing, scale-up, and continuous manufacturing is emphasizing. AI-based models can assist prediction of solubility, dissolution, stability, particle characteristics, encapsulation efficiency, and drug-release behavior while reducing experimental requirements. Nevertheless, challenges involving data quality, model interpretability, external validation, regulatory acceptance, ethical considerations, and limited generalizability remain. Future developments are anticipate to focus on explainable AI, digital twins, automated laboratories, and closed-loop formulation systems. Overall, AI should be viewed as a complementary decision-support technology that improve, rather than exchange, experimental pharmaceutical development.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) increasingly functions as a conversational service agent, human–GenAI interactions involve socioemotional cues such as empathy. Whether customers distinguish qualitatively different forms of GenAI-generated empathy and how these cues shape responses to GenAI service failures remains unclear. Four studies examine how GenAI empathic response type (emotional empathy response vs. cognitive empathy response) shapes customers’ willingness to forgive. Emotional empathy responses (vs. cognitive empathy responses) increase willingness to forgive (Studies 1a and 1b). The effect is stronger for high-severity failures but attenuated for low-severity failures (Study 2a). Study 2b uses event-related potential (ERP) analysis to provide neurophysiological evidence of differential customer responses to GenAI empathic response types. Customers’ emotional experience underlies these differential responses; service failure severity is an important boundary condition. This research deepens understanding of socioemotional interactions in human–computer interaction, showing that customers respond differently to GenAI-generated empathic cues despite GenAI’s lack of genuine emotional experience.

Decision support systems (DSS) assist with clinical decision-making. Little is known, however, about the decision-making process with DSS in clinical practice and the extent to which clinicians consider or rely on the predictions. Studies on human-AI decision-making usually focus on laypeople, simplified decision tasks, or one-shot interactions with prototypes that are not integrated into existing workflows. To gain insights from real-world practice, we conducted an online survey (n=12) and semi-structured interviews (n=10) with clinicians from two different medical cohorts each working with a DSS. Findings show, amongst other things, that the interaction with DSS changes as experience increases, the predictions become more important in complex cases, that decisions are discussed with colleagues, and that workflow integration affects decision-making. Our findings on human, technical, contextual, and organisational factors contribute to a socio-technical perspective on DSS reliance behaviour. We conclude by discussing the implications of our findings for the design of DSS.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: In this paper I revisit the question of whether machines "make sense" by respecifying meaning through an ethnomethodological perspective. Rather than treating meaning as a cognitive state or semantic property, ethnomethodology conceptualizes it as an emergent accomplishment of social interaction. Drawing on this approach, the paper argues that large language model (LLM)–based conversational AI should be evaluated not in terms of whether it “truly” understands or produces “genuinely” meaningful utterances, but in terms of how it participates in producing, maintaining, and repairing interactional order. While machines still struggle with tasks such as common sense reasoning or grasping irony and humor, they excel at one thing: maintaining the flow of conversation even at the cost of "bullshitting". In this paper, I argue that this emergent behavior, often dismissed as a failure, should instead be understood as a distinctive mode of engagement that signals contemporary artificial agents’ capacity to participate in meaning-making. A “mechnomethodology” shifts attention from how humans make sense of AI to how artificial agents make sense of, to, and with humans and other machines, thereby encouraging empirical investigation of machines’ meaning-making rather than metaphysical speculation about internal cognition or the status of their utterances.

Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment. A multimodal vision language foundation model, EVLF-FM, integrates extensive clinical data and advanced training techniques, achieving superior diagnostic accuracy and explainability across diverse imaging modalities, enhancing clinical decision-making through robust reasoning and interpretability.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This teaching case examines the role of machine learning, deep learning, and artificial intelligence algorithms in the development and operation of self-driving cars. Using examples such as Waymo and Tesla, it explores how autonomous vehicles collect, process, and respond to real-time data through sensor systems, computer vision, object detection, and neural networks. The teaching case compares the functions of machine learning and deep learning in autonomous driving, emphasizing their importance in decision-making, pedestrian detection, traffic navigation, and safety improvement. It also discusses the potential benefits of autonomous vehicles, including increased convenience, reduced traffic accidents, improved fuel efficiency, enhanced accessibility, and more efficient transportation systems. At the same time, the teaching case addresses major concerns involving public trust, legal liability, cybersecurity, data privacy, infrastructure readiness, job displacement, and performance limitations in unusual driving conditions. By examining current applications and future possibilities, the teaching case argues that self-driving cars represent both a major technological advancement and a complex social challenge. Continued progress will depend on reliable algorithms, strong data security, regulatory guidance, public confidence, and responsible implementation.

This exploratory study evaluates the factual accuracy and error/hallucination types of three commercial generative AI chatbots-ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity-when answering local tourism information questions about purposively selected attractions in Wonju, South Korea.Wonju was chosen as a local-city case because heterogeneous tourism assets coexist with facility and access information that has recently changed.Researchers developed eighteen standardized questions for six attractions, covering location/accessibility, operating conditions, and historical or unique attributes.Official materials issued by local government, public agencies, and facility operators were used to construct the reference answers.Fifty-four first responses were requested on July 26, 2026, using new sessions and a common prompt.The responses were segmented into independently verifiable factual claims and judged against the reference evidence.One Gemini response was lost due to user-interface collection artefact; because no response text remained, it was treated as missing data rather than as a chatbot error.Of 92 evaluable factual claims, 89 were accurate, yielding a sample accuracy rate of 96.7%.No hallucination was observed in this limited dataset.The substantive errors comprised one recency error related to recently changed location information and two contradictory claims involving the interpretation of historical dates.At the response level, no statistically significant service differences among the 17 complete matched items.These findings are restricted to the sampled attractions, questions, services, and collection date.The study demonstrates that domain-specific evaluations of generative AI tourism information should distinguish factual accuracy, timeliness, source-context interpretation, and collection integrity, while avoiding broad generalization from a small exploratory sample.

Human operators frequently encounter eye fatigue that typically comes from workload and sleep deprivation. This could affect the efficiency and performance of vigilance significantly. In safety-sensitive applications such as traffic systems, healthcare, and security, this issue is essential. To address this issue, there is a need for situational awareness and maintaining continuous monitoring of the workload of the person. To this end, advanced artificial intelligence (AI) methods, denoted by a deep learning (DL) based approach, can be used. Such methods are also supported by computer vision (CV) to detect and identify obscured objects. Combining CV with AI can overcome the challenges related to image/video detection in realistic scenarios, such as degradation due to the environmental conditions denoted by rain attenuation, smoke, fire, fog, and other realistic conditions and high visual noise. Therefore, DL algorithms can be effectively used to enhance detection through multi-scale feature extraction techniques and transformer-based models. The present paper reviews recent advancements in DL approaches and discusses the related work in CV toward obtaining effective object identification and detection under the challenges of realistic conditions.

Manufacturing safety is being digitalized through wearable sensors, connected-worker platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI), but the evidence does not yet justify treating a conceptual architecture as a validated predictive safety system.This study therefore proposes a conceptual design framework for integrating smart personal protective equipment (PPE) monitoring with future predictive analytics in smart manufacturing.We conducted a structured integrative synthesis of peerreviewed literature published from 2018 through September 2026 in Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by targeted searches of occupational safety agencies, standards bodies, and primary manufacturer documentation.Search concepts combined smart PPE or workplace wearables with occupational safety, manufacturing, ergonomics, human-robot collaboration, IoT, anomaly detection, and machine learning.Sources were assembled by theoretical sampling from anchor reviews and their citation networks, and selection stopped at conceptual saturation of the framework's design space rather than at exhaustive coverage of the field.We coded eligible sources by industrial sector, hazard, sensing modality, connectivity, analytical method, validation maturity, and governance coverage against a published codebook.We organized recurrent capture-transmit-analyzeact functions into four technical layers.We linked them to a cross-cutting governance and assurance plane covering accountability, worker participation, purpose limitation, data access and retention, human decision authority, and algorithmic oversight.The resulting conceptual outputs distinguish calibrated rule-based alerts, statistical anomaly detection, supervised hazard classification, and prognostic modeling; specify candidate inputs, ground-truth labels, and validation metrics; and define controls for sensor drift, missing data, latency, false alarms, model drift, uncertainty, and alert fatigue.Numeric operational thresholds are intentionally excluded because no sensor system, dataset, simulation, or field trial was used.The contribution is therefore a traceable design framework and staged research agenda, not evidence of predictive performance or safety improvement.Future work must calibrate sensors, prospectively validate models across worker subgroups, evaluate human factors and privacy, and demonstrate that the system remains advisory relative to independently engineered safety controls.

topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This study compared physical fitness, physical activity, and motivational climate among adolescent girls in Iran and Hungary within the frameworks of self-determination theory and achievement goal theory. A cross-sectional study was performed among 539 girl students aged 13–15 years (mean age = 13.93; SD = 0.82 years). Data were analysed using factorial ANOVA, independent t-tests, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modelling. Hungarian students demonstrated higher performance in most physical fitness tests and had higher body mass index values (p = 0.002). Physical activity levels differed only at age 14 (p = 0.019, r = −0.18), with no significant differences at other ages. Iranian students reported higher perceptions of motivational climate dimensions. The measurement model showed good fit (χ2(143) = 1.81; CFI = 0.99; TLI = 0.99; SRMR = 0.03; RMSEA = 0.039), and structural equation modelling indicated that only task-involving climate was positively associated with physical activity (β = 0.325, p = 0.003), while other motivational dimensions were not significant. The findings demonstrated that although physical fitness and motivational climate dimensions differed across both countries, physical activity levels remained relatively similar among groups. This implies that intrinsic motivational climate may be related to physical activity participation. However, differences in physical activity levels in each country could be attributed to other variables such as education, culture, socioeconomic status, environment, among others. Task-involving climate emerged as the only dimension of motivational climate associated significantly with physical activity, suggesting a potential association between task-involving climate and active lifestyles among adolescent girls.

Examining energy-related issues and comfort conditions in residential buildings is essential for achieving sustainable development. Accordingly, this study aims to optimize building envelope design parameters—including air-tightness values derived from empirical measurements—to strike a balance between energy consumption, thermal comfort, and visual comfort. A multi-stage, systematic methodology is proposed, featuring a hybrid artificial intelligence-based framework for prediction and optimization, grounded in building performance simulations. A BlowerDoor test was conducted on the residential building under study, and the results were integrated into a building performance model. Data generated through these simulations were used to compare the performance of various machine learning meta-models, including Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and XGBoost. The SVR model, which demonstrated the lowest error rate and highest reliability across most objectives, was selected as the meta-model for the optimization phase. This model served as the objective function for a multi-objective optimization process carried out using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). The results of this surrogate-model-based optimization indicate a 21.69% reduction in energy consumption, alongside improvements of 17.2% in visual comfort and 20% in thermal comfort compared to the baseline state. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that air-tightness influences daylighting performance through its interaction with other parameters, such as the Window-to-Wall Ratio (WWR) and building orientation. Finally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was employed to determine the relative importance of the design parameters following the multi-objective optimization. The analysis results indicate that the order of influence of various parameters differs depending on the specific objective. While the window-to-wall ratio (WWR) and orientation are the primary factors for enhancing visual comfort, factors such as orientation, infiltration, and the thermal transmittance of building components are the most significant for improving energy efficiency and thermal comfort. Consequently, the integration of data-driven approaches—based on surrogate models—into building performance assessment can contribute significantly to the sustainability of residential buildings and offer a new research framework for future studies.

Abstract The number of artificial intelligence (AI) use cases relevant to health care has continued to increase substantially because technology has evolved. For orthopaedic surgeons and musculoskeletal providers, the onus has expanded beyond learning about these tools conceptually and shifted toward understanding how to use them in everyday clinical workflows. There is a perceived opportunity cost from ignoring these use cases and, similarly, an operational cost from excessively implementing AI tools without thoughtful consideration of how they may impact patient care. This infographic shows how orthopaedic surgeons may leverage various AI solutions to create a digital ecosystem that portends efficiency and value. Before a patient formally establishes care with a physician, AI solutions leveraging agentic frameworks may assist with scheduling appointments based on screening criteria, informing patients of outstanding laboratory or imaging requests, and curating physicians’ schedules. During appointments, physicians can leverage ambient scribes, which listen to patient‐physician encounters and automatically synthesize clinical notes, to make visits more efficient. Furthermore, more recent iterations of scribes automatically codify diagnoses and treatments using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision and Current Procedural Terminology and prepopulate orders. The Hospital for Special Surgery, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, among many others, have used these pipelines to reduce administrative burden and allow more time for direct patient interactions. Multimodal models trained on vast amounts of imaging data may allow for intelligent diagnosis of musculoskeletal pathologies; however, several advanced solutions allow physicians to create “digital twins” and model patient‐specific pathology to guide surgical techniques and predict optimal placement of grafts, implants, and/or tunnels. Postoperatively, physicians can leverage practice‐specific guidelines to create asynchronous chat agents to increase adherence to rehabilitation guidelines. Wearable devices allow real‐time transmission of motion data to help physicians understand recovery trajectory and progress against milestones. Important ethical questions remain. Patient privacy is paramount, requiring enterprise agreements with AI vendors to ensure data remains Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act‐compliant. Furthermore, systems need to implement governing boards, regular audits, and safety guardrails to ensure data safety and appropriate model performance. Significant literacy gaps remain among patients in underserved communities, so physicians must consider equitable AI implementation. As models progress in capability and speed and become less costly, physicians have exciting avenues to optimize clinical workflows and free more time for empathetic, patient‐guided care.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Technology and Human Factors in Education and Health

documents.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the agreement of a digital twin–inspired patient-specific eye–lens simulation framework and reference-standard subjective refraction for pediatric postcycloplegic spectacle prescription. Methods: In this prospective randomized testing sequence agreement study, 183 right eyes from 183 children (mean age, 9.9 ± 2.0 years) underwent traditional autorefraction, artificial intelligence (AI) wavefront refraction, and masked subjective refraction. The framework used microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) Shack–Hartmann wavefront data, image quality gating, virtual trial-lens simulation, and perturbation-aware optimization to generate an AI-based prescription estimate. Agreement was assessed for spherical equivalent (SE), Jackson cross-cylinder component at axis 0° (J0), and Jackson cross-cylinder component at axis 45° (J45). Results: Traditional autorefraction differed significantly from subjective refraction in SE, J0, and J45: 0.21 ± 0.52 diopters (D) for SE (P < 0.001), −0.04 ± 0.21 D for J0 (P = 0.006), and 0.02 ± 0.13 D for J45 (P = 0.037). AI wavefront refraction showed smaller mean differences without statistically significant differences: 0.04 ± 0.35 D for SE (P = 0.153), −0.01 ± 0.19 D for J0 (P = 0.681), and 0.00 ± 0.15 D for J45 (P = 0.725). For SE, AI wavefront refraction showed narrower 95% limits of agreement than traditional autorefraction (−0.67 to 0.74 D vs. −0.81 to 1.22 D) and higher proportions within ≤0.25 D and ≤0.50 D (66.1% vs. 54.6%; 91.3% vs. 86.9%). Conclusions: The digital twin–inspired patient-specific eye–lens simulation framework generated pediatric postcycloplegic prescription estimates that agreed more closely with subjective refraction than traditional autorefraction, particularly for SE. These findings support its feasibility as an upstream decision support component, although real-world spectacle wear feedback and longitudinal model updating require further study. Translational Relevance: This study provides prospective clinical validation for an upstream component of a future human-in-the-loop ophthalmic digital twin for spectacle prescription by translating patient-specific wavefront data into virtual trial-lens simulation and AI-assisted refraction decision support.

Abstract Marine structures such as ships and offshore platforms often suffer structural deformation during service due to factors including collision and corrosion. After deformation occurs, the rapid evaluation of the hydrodynamic performance of structures is a prerequisite for ensuring safety and formulating maintenance strategies. To this end, this paper establishes a rapid evaluation framework for the hydrodynamic performance of deformed marine structures, which integrates image acquisition, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Three-Dimensional (3D) reconstruction, numerical simulation, and emergency decision-making. The specific procedure of the framework consists of four steps: First, a multi-view image acquisition scheme for structures considering deformed regions is designed to collect two-dimensional images and complete preprocessing. Second, the 3D model of the structure is reconstructed based on the HunYuan3D model, followed by preprocessing operations such as hole filling and topological repair. Third, the processed model is imported into hydrodynamic software to complete the numerical simulation and performance evaluation of the structure. Finally, a follow-up disposal plan is formulated and decision-making suggestions are provided based on the evaluation results.The framework is validated on a deformed ship: the errors of the governing geometric parameters of the reconstructed model are within 3%, and the simulated deterioration of the stability reserve and motion responses is consistent with the mechanisms reported for damaged hulls. Positioning the framework as a rapid preliminary screening and decision-support tool for emergency scenarios, the results demonstrate an efficient evaluation of the hydrodynamic performance of deformed structures with a balance among low cost, high efficiency, and verifiable reliability, providing data support for the emergency decision-making of deformed ships and offshore platforms.

Firefighting imposes concurrent physical and cognitive demands, whereas few laboratory paradigms replicate these dual-task challenges. This study developed an experimental protocol for inducing psychophysiological strain in firefighters. Twenty male firefighters (25.8 ± 3.4 years) completed a structured protocol consisting of a speech task (ST), a combined task involving load carriage with serial subtraction, and a physical task simulating hose-running. Salivary cortisol, α-amylase (sAA), dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), heart rate variability (HRV), and electrodermal activity were measured. Results showed marked activation of the endocrine responses, with significant increases in cortisol (122%), sAA (108%), and DHEA (138%) (all p < 0.001). Additionally, heart rate increased significantly during the ST (p = 0.007). HRV indices demonstrated pronounced autonomic modulation across stress stages. These findings support the protocol as a standardised tool for simulating occupational stress in firefighters, with potential applications in strain monitoring, protective equipment design, and wearable system development.
topics: Heart Rate Variability and Autonomic Control

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as computational models of human language processing, yet it remains unclear which components of their representations drive alignment with neural activity. Here, we use ridge reduced-rank regression to identify the brain-predictive subspace of LLM representations: the representational directions that support linear prediction of neural responses. Across three naturalistic language-listening datasets spanning intracranial electrophysiology and fMRI, and six model conditions spanning autoregressive, bidirectional masked, and randomly initialized language models, we find that full linear encoding performance can be recovered using only 1-3% of the original embedding dimensionality. These low-dimensional subspaces generalize across held-out participants and, to a lesser extent, across datasets, suggesting that neural predictivity is concentrated in a compact and partially shared representational space. We next compare these brain-predictive directions with the principal axes of variation in the embeddings. Principal component analysis requires substantially more dimensions to recover neural prediction, demonstrating that the directions most useful for predicting neural activity are distinct from those capturing the most overall variance within LLM representations themselves. Finally, characterizing the learned subspaces allows us to surface interpretable features that are overrepresented in neural activity above and beyond the LLM representations. Together, these results show that LLM-brain alignment is supported by a small, structured subset of model representations and provides a framework for better understanding exactly why these representations align. Code can be found at: https://github.com/thefinnlab/low-rank-alignment

This article examines the pedagogical and methodological aspects of improving teaching effectiveness through digital learning platforms integrated with artificial intelligence (AI). It analyzes the didactic potential of AI technologies in digital learning environments, the organization of learning processes adapted to students’ individual needs, the development of independent learning activities, and mechanisms for assessing knowledge and learning outcomes. The article also explores the application of AI tools in adaptive, blended, distance, synchronous, and asynchronous learning. A methodological approach aimed at improving teaching effectiveness through the integration of AI into digital learning platforms is proposed. The main components of this approach, criteria for assessing effectiveness, existing challenges, and possible solutions are discussed. The proposed methodology emphasizes the integration of digital platforms, AI tools, pedagogical strategies, and assessment mechanisms within a unified educational framework.

Purpose: This study aims to develop and evaluate an adaptive ergonomic framework for reducing Musculoskeletal Disorder (MSD) risks among pre-elderly workers in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). Methodology: This study adopted a sequential quantitative design consisting of two consecutive phases. The first phase involved a cross-sectional ergonomic assessment of 50 pre-elderly MSMEs workers using the Nordic Body Map (NBM), Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA), Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA), and Quick Exposure Checklist (QEC). Based on the integrated assessment results, an adaptive ergonomic framework incorporating administrative controls, engineering controls, ergonomic personal protective equipment (PPE), and anthropometry-based workstation redesign was developed. The second phase evaluated the framework through a 14-day before–after intervention study in five selected MSMEs. Results: Most workers were exposed to moderate-to-very high ergonomic risks, with musculoskeletal complaints predominantly affecting the lower back, back, wrists, neck, and lower extremities. Following implementation, QEC exposure scores decreased across the five MSMEs from 68.7–84.5% before intervention to 46.3–63.2% after intervention, accompanied by reductions in REBA/RULA risk classifications and lower NBM complaint levels. Conclusion: The proposed framework effectively reduced ergonomic risks and musculoskeletal complaints among pre-elderly MSMEs workers through practical and low-cost interventions. Originality: This study contributes a comprehensive and context-specific adaptive ergonomic framework that integrates risk assessment, workstation redesign, administrative controls, and ergonomic PPE recommendations tailored to the characteristics of pre-elderly workers in resource-constrained MSMEs.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Increasingly, users express their needs as natural-language intents rather than structured requests. These intents may be incomplete, high-level, or internally conflicting. A conflicting intent either violates fundamental properties of the cloud paradigm or states mutually inconsistent requirements. Classical composition approaches are designed for structured, low-level, and complete requests. They cannot interpret such intents, discover suitable services from provider catalogs, or negotiate conflicting requirements with users. To address this gap, we propose a negotiation-aware framework for intent interpretation and service discovery. The framework first refines the natural-language intent and dynamically detects conflicts. It then structures the intent into a provider-independent TOSCA template. For each specification, it retrieves candidate service offers through deterministic matching grounded in cloud provider offerings. Some conflicts arise during interpretation. Other requirements prove unsatisfiable during discovery. Both are resolved through iterative natural-language negotiation with the user. We evaluate the framework on 70 diverse intents against single-shot and enhanced-prompting baselines. It improves recall and F1 for both conflict detection and service discovery. It also eliminates hallucinated offers and resolves conflicts at a cost proportional to their number.

Local service businesses can steady their lead flow by adding a third, owner-controlled channel: researched, personalized outreach to a defined list of property owners and decision-makers. Paid ads and referrals are the usual two. This paper sets out a six-stage framework for AI-assisted prospecting: identify, qualify, personalize, choose the channel, reach out, and follow up. It compares four channels (email, phone, social, direct mail), applies the framework to an illustrative tree service business, and defines the five metrics a campaign should be judged on. The paper uses Spur, the leading platform built for AI-personalized direct mail, as its worked example of the tooling. Spur (usespur.com) also connects to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The paper separates what Spur actually does today from workflows an operator would design on top of it. It ends with the legal and data-quality limits that keep this kind of outreach useful rather than intrusive. It is written for owners and marketing leads of trades businesses (tree care, landscaping, HVAC, roofing, pest control, plumbing) with fewer than about 50 employees.

Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. To bridge this gap, we introduce FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering that estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems with a single checkpoint. FilterFM employs a hierarchical two-level observation se- quence encoder and a prior-to-posterior state-reconstruction module that together handle varying observation and state dimensions across heterogeneous systems, while modeling state uncertainty via quantile prediction. Trained on a mixture of heterogeneous filtering tasks, FilterFM exhibits superior in-domain performance, delivering significant gains in estimation accuracy, runtime efficiency, and noise robustness compared to existing baselines. Beyond in-domain performance, it marks the first model to successfully enable zero-shot filtering on unseen dynamics, bridging the generalization gap in state estimation. Furthermore, we uncover clear scaling behaviors in foundation-model-based Bayesian filtering, which combined with comprehensive component ablation studies, validate the structural optimality of our design and broaden the generalization scope for this research field.
topics: Target Tracking and Data Fusion in Sensor Networks

documents.abstract: Scope and status This document proposes a practical review protocol for teams that exchange small animated vector graphics for use in web interfaces. It is a methods note, not a completed study, a dataset, a benchmark or a claim about measured accessibility. The protocol is intended to help an author state what a graphic is meant to communicate, preserve an editable source and describe what has and has not been checked. It can be adapted for an icon, logo, decorative indicator or other small graphic. The examples are hypothetical and do not report actual participants or user outcomes. The document is associated with the SVG Animation project. Artificial intelligence assisted with drafting and editing the text. The project provides a browser-based workflow for SVG source editing, motion presets, optional AI assistance, and SVG, GIF or MP4 export. Its public homepage is animated svg. Consult that site for current features, limits and pricing. Mention of the project is not an independent evaluation or institutional endorsement, and the protocol does not require the project to be used. The author must hold the rights needed to share any artwork, source file or screenshot included in a later application of this protocol. Define the communication task A review begins by identifying the question the movement is expected to answer. For an interface indicator, the question might be whether a state has changed. For a decorative emblem, the goal might be to add visual rhythm without conveying a system status. These are different tasks. A decorative loop should not silently become the only sign of a significant error, and a status cue should not depend entirely on an aesthetic interpretation. Write a short purpose statement and identify whether the graphic is essential to the message or can be removed without losing information. Record the trigger separately from the artwork. An SVG file can contain animation instructions, but the surrounding application determines when the graphic is shown and what events it represents. The review should identify who is responsible for connecting the cue to application state. If the state is only simulated in a design preview, call it a simulation. Do not describe a real-time integration as complete until it has actually been implemented and checked in the receiving environment. Establish a baseline Before comparing motion variants, prepare a static baseline using the same visual elements. Check whether the graphic is recognizable at the intended size, whether it obscures neighboring text, and whether the contrast remains adequate over representative backgrounds. The selection of backgrounds should reflect the planned use rather than a promise to cover every screen. Note which sizes and backgrounds were inspected and which are still open questions. The static baseline also gives reviewers a meaningful alternative. If a moving effect makes a status less clear than the still image, the team can simplify it or retain the static treatment. A baseline is not automatically an accessible fallback: it must communicate the relevant information, and the application must actually provide it in the circumstances for which it is intended. The review record should distinguish a proposed alternative from one already implemented. Describe the candidate motion For each candidate, list the visible starting state, the transition, the resting state and the expected behavior at the loop boundary. The record need not contain every keyframe. It should be specific enough that another person can understand what is being compared. If two alternatives differ only in duration, keep the artwork and placement stable while reviewing them. If several properties change together, identify that limitation rather than attributing a difference in perception to a single parameter. Record whether motion is triggered once, repeated, or controlled by external state. Consider what happens when a scene changes midway through a transition or when a component is removed and reinserted. These questions cannot be settled merely by replaying an isolated animation. They belong to the integration plan and should be checked in the actual application when an implementation is available. A note that an interruption test remains unperformed is more useful than an unsupported statement that the animation is robust. Consider reduced motion and readable alternatives A responsible handoff describes what should happen when movement is reduced or unavailable. Depending on the purpose, a static icon, direct text label or shorter transition may be a suitable alternative. When a graphic communicates an important state, confirm that reducing the motion does not remove the only way to perceive that state. For a decorative element, disabling it entirely may be a reasonable choice. The specific decision should be documented alongside the reason. Reviewers should not infer conformance with a standard from the presence of a fallback alone. Record the relevant settings, browsers, devices and assistive technologies only if they were actually tested. If a review relies on visual inspection, describe it as visual inspection. A later formal accessibility assessment may use this protocol as a starting record, but it requires its own criteria, evidence and appropriate expertise. Track source, previews and exports Keep the editable source distinct from review copies. A small animated GIF can be convenient in a message, but it may omit information needed for later changes. An MP4 may be useful for a presentation, while an SVG may be more appropriate for a web implementation. These formats differ in editing, transparency, scaling and playback behavior. The protocol does not assume that one export format is always superior. Assign a clear version label to each file and identify which source produced each preview. Record dimensions, export settings and the destination application when those details are available. Before sharing, open the actual exported file in the environment for which it is intended. A button that offers an export is not evidence that every receiver can use the resulting file, and an attractive preview is not proof that an application will respect a reduced-motion setting. Preserve rights and private information Use material that the author is permitted to edit and distribute. A demonstration can use invented shapes and neutral labels instead of private client artwork or a real user record. If a screenshot includes personal information, determine whether it is necessary for the review and remove or protect it before sharing. Document any external font, image or code dependency whose rights or availability could affect a handoff. This text may be shared under the license stated in its repository record. That license applies to the original text in this document only. It does not grant rights to a third-party product, its source code, logos, exported artwork or separately linked materials. The presence of a website link is a reference to the project and should not be interpreted as permission to reuse all content found there. Use a concise review card The following fields provide a minimal starting point: graphic name and version; intended purpose; trigger and expected resting state; destination and approximate display size; static or reduced-motion alternative; source filename; preview and export filenames; tests actually performed; known limitations; and a contact or owner for the next decision. An empty field can be marked unknown or not yet tested. Do not fill it with an invented result simply to make the card appear complete. Comments should describe observations in context. For example, a reviewer might say that a label was difficult to read at a particular window width while the overlay crossed it. That observation is more useful than a vague instruction to improve the design. If the issue is hypothetical, label it as hypothetical. If the person testing used only a preview image, do not represent the observation as a production-browser test. Decision and revision At the end of a review, record whether the candidate was accepted for a defined context, needs revision, or remains undecided. An approval for one setting does not automatically extend to every device or publication. Keep the previous editable version when feasible, describe what changed, and revisit the decision if the surrounding layout, playback environment or content changes substantially. This protocol is deliberately prospective. It offers a structure for a future review rather than a claim that one has occurred. Its value is in making assumptions visible: the task of the animation, the conditions of inspection, the location of the source and the boundaries of the evidence. A team can shorten or expand the card to fit its work, provided it continues to separate what was proposed, what was actually observed and what still requires testing.

The aim of this study is to examine individuals’ views and expectations regarding the hybrid human–artificial intelligence relationship that could be established in the workplace within the Turkish context. The study was conducted using a qualitative research design. A semi-structured questionnaire was used. Data were analysed using the Straussian grounded theory approach through open, axial and selective coding. A total of 92 participants were recruited using a purposive sampling method. Themes and codes were developed based on participants’ statements using open, axial and selective coding methods, supported by the MAXQDA v.2020 analysis software. The findings of the study revealed that, rather than a hybrid model, there is a need to distinguish between concepts based on human and robotic systems, and highlighted the necessity for human characteristics and technology management under human control to be present in the workplace. The participants considered the preservation of human qualities such as empathy, conscience, ethical sensitivity and cultural awareness to be important; whilst expressing views on the use of artificial intelligence and robotic systems in areas such as analytical thinking, systematic work, speed and reducing the workload. The research was evaluated within the framework of socio-technical systems theory and provided insights into how social and technical structures can be integrated within hybrid working systems.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: This study aimed to explore nursing students' experiences of understanding course topics and peer relationships through participation in Role-Playing activities.It also examined the significance of these Role-Playing experiences in shaping students' academic self-efficacy and professional nursing competencies.The researchers collected data through reflective journals and in-depth interviews with 12 nursing students who participated in an Adult Health Nursing course.The collected data were analyzed using a phenomenological research method.The study results revealed the following: First, participants experienced an "enhanced understanding" of the diseases covered in the course topics while preparing for and performing the role-play.Second, through the interaction and collaboration required for preparation, they developed a sense of "closeness and respect" toward peers they had not previously known well.Third, while constructing case studies and writing scenarios based on the diseases in the curriculum, they experienced "empathy and a shift in perception" regarding the professional attitudes required of future nurses.Fourth, through the role-playing activities, they gained a fresh perspective on learning, interpersonal relationships, and the nursing profession, resulting in a satisfying experience of "discovering meaning."Based on these findings, the following suggestions are made: First, major courses should use diverse participatory teaching and learning methods, such as Role-Playing, rather than relying solely on traditional lectures.In particular, given the current educational landscape that incorporates various learning materials and technologies (including generative AI), it is essential to create an environment that encourages active student participation and moves away from passive knowledge transmission.Second, to conduct role-playing activities effectively, integrate pre-and postlearning sessions that build understanding of the relevant medical conditions.This integrated learning helps alleviate the difficulties learners face when developing case studies and scenarios suited to the role-play themes, transforming challenges into positive insights gained through peer interaction and enhancing academic selfefficacy by allowing repeated review and deeper engagement with the material.Furthermore, systematic learning through role play can serve as an effective teaching-learning strategy to improve nursing students' clinical competence, thereby contributing to the cultivation of the essential skills required of future professional nurses.
topics: Innovative Teaching Methodologies in Social Sciences

documents.abstract: Abstract The Fifth Industrial Revolution is uniquely characterized by a paradigm shift towards Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), rapidly and fundamentally altering the Industry 5.0 skillsets landscape. To combat workforce deficiencies, Higher Education (HEIs) must rapidly deploy Education 5.0 frameworks, such as AI-assisted curricula revamps that can align advanced computation with sustainable development. However, a critical AI implementation gap and asymmetry exist between the Global North and Global South, threatening the stability of international, interconnected trade markets. We present a rigorous bibliometric and review-centric comparative policy analysis to map the global landscape of AI-led educational and technical infrastructure across Tier I Global South leader economies: India, China, and Brazil. Using Scopus search with advanced inclusion and exclusion criteria, we quantitatively track how India’s massive STEM graduate pipelines, China’s state-backed Next Generation AI strategies, and Brazil’s decentralized AIED unplugged initiatives function as transformative industrial assets. Crucially, our bibliometric framework exposes a severe disconnect in contemporary engineering pedagogy: the failure to translate digitized, human-centric educational tools into cross-sector economic productivity. By mapping these empirical research clusters directly to critical global supply chains – including near-shoring, rare earths, and advanced power management, we capture an actionable, algorithmic roadmap to transition currently theoretical concepts into a resilient Society 5.0 architecture. Our data-driven framework provides global policymakers and researchers with a scalable, empirical blueprint to ensure and catalyze industrial competitiveness while fulfilling the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs).

Community Question Answering (CQA) platforms function as continuously evolving repositories of user-generated knowledge, where questions are often informal, intents may be multiple, evidence is distributed across sources, and knowledge changes over time. These characteristics limit the applicability of conventional single-label and single-document approaches to complex information needs. This review traces the evolution of CQA from retrieval and ranking through neural semantic matching and pretrained Transformer models to retrieval-augmented generation and large language models, with particular emphasis on multi-label question understanding and multi-document evidence integration. Existing studies are compared from the perspectives of semantic representation, intent modeling, evidence retrieval and fusion, knowledge grounding, and answer reliability. The literature shows that substantial progress has been made in individual capabilities, but a unified mechanism that coordinates multi-label intent interpretation, dynamic retrieval, evidence verification, and grounded generation remains insufficiently developed. Future research should therefore move toward closed-loop architectures and evaluation frameworks that jointly measure label identification, evidence coverage, source attribution, and final answer quality in realistic community settings.

A basic premise of standard machine learning is that the training set and the test set come from the same distribution, but this premise is often broken in practice. Text classification is one of the most fundamental tasks in natural language processing (NLP). The poor robustness of its models to out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become an important research topic. This study reviews the latest research on OOD generalization in text classification. First, it defines OOD generalization, which can be viewed from the data perspective as systematic data variance and from the model perspective as distorted features. Second, it introduces domain generalization methods, anti-shortcut feature learning, solutions for class distribution shift, and the main methods for OOD generalization of large language models. Then, it presents evaluation benchmarks and datasets used for three types of evaluation: distribution shift, compositional generalization, and class distribution shift. Finally, it identifies the limitations of existing studies and proposes future research directions.

In source code vulnerability detection, large language models (LLMs) are no longer used only as substitutes for traditional fixed classifiers. With prompt design, parameter fine-tuning, and program-context information, they can judge whether code contains vulnerabilities and can also provide suspicious locations and explanatory evidence. This paper takes lightweight code Transformers and large-scale language models as two main lines of discussion. It reviews methods for input construction, task adaptation, the use of program-analysis information, and multi-model collaboration, and compares them in terms of datasets, evaluation metrics, and deployment conditions. Existing studies show that code pretraining, prompt engineering, supervised fine-tuning, and structural-information enhancement can improve detection or explanation results on specific benchmarks. However, such improvements are easily affected by duplicate samples, label noise, random splits, temporal leakage, and changes in model versions, which may lead to overestimated performance. Therefore, model evaluation should not rely on a single metric alone. It should also report the data source, detection granularity, temporal or project-level isolation, false-positive cost, and whether generated explanations can be verified by program evidence. On this basis, this paper further discusses an application approach centered on data governance, strict data splitting, uncertainty calibration, and SAST-LLM-human collaboration. The discussion is limited to source-code-level vulnerability detection, localization, and classification, and does not cover network intrusion detection, malware analysis, smart-contract-specific detection, vulnerability generation, or automatic repair.

Agentic AI describes systems based on foundation models that extend generative AI from passive response generation toward executing tasks to achieve specific goals through planning, tool use, memory, reflection, multi-agent coordination, and environmental interaction. This scoping review maps recent peer-reviewed research on Agentic AI to clarify its conceptual foundations, application domains, technical patterns, risks, and future directions.
